The graph-theoretic framework we introduce may be useful more widely in the design and analysis of correlated strategies for rendezvous.
item.dc:creator: Javier Cembrano, Felix Fischer, Max Klimm

item.title: Transferability of Error Bounds and the Kurdyka-\L ojasiewicz Property under $C^1$ Partial Smoothness
item.description: arXiv:2605.02754v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This work studies how a generalized error bound (GEB) property in the ambient Euclidean space transfers to the active manifold under $C^1$ partial smoothness. The GEB generalizes the standard error bound, which upper bounds the distance to a subset of critical points using first-order stationarity residuals, by allowing the distance to be composed with a gauge function. In the ambient space, these residuals are measured by the subdifferential or the slope of the original function, while on the manifold they are measured by the Riemannian gradient or the slope of the restricted function. We develop complementary geometric and metric analyses to show that the ambient and manifold GEBs are equivalent with the same gauge function. The geometric argument shows that the projection of the subdifferential onto the tangent space coincides with the Riemannian gradient, while the metric approach combines slope estimates, identifiability, and a new uniform linear-growth result for $C^1$ manifolds. We further extend our analysis to establish the analogous equivalence for the Kurdyka--\L ojasiewicz (KL) property, with the same desingularizer, and separately characterize their connections with the GEB. Finally, for regularized optimization, we relate subdifferential and proximal error bounds, thereby placing the previously established equivalence between proximal and manifold error bounds for $\ell_1$-regularization within a broader framework.
item.dc:creator: Hanju Wu, Ching-pei Lee, Yue Xie

item.title: Kernel-based potential mean-field games with unbiased random Fourier $U$-statistics
item.description: arXiv:2605.29371v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the subclass of potential mean-field games in which the running interaction cost and the terminal target cost are both expressed through reproducing-kernel maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) penalties, and develop a computational framework that exploits this kernel structure. Both costs are estimated from finite-sample empirical distributions using a random Fourier U-statistic representation that is unbiased and has linear cost in the batch size. The drift of the controlled diffusion is parametrized by a neural network and trained via stochastic gradient descent. For population near-minimizers we prove convergence to the terminal-constrained problem as the penalty diverges, and show that the same limit is recovered almost surely when such controls are evaluated on independent finite samples under explicit coupling conditions on the penalty, random-feature count and sample size. The framework includes the kernel-MMD-penalty Schr{\"o}dinger bridge problem as the special case of a vanishing interaction cost. Numerical experiments illustrate the method on the Schr{\"o}dinger bridge problem in dimensions up to one hundred, and on an electric vehicle charging coordination problem with per-vehicle physical heterogeneity, where a control-dependent aggregate-demand cost produces a trade-off between peak normalized charging power and the terminal service level.
item.dc:creator: Yumiharu Nakano

item.title: Optimal Oracle Complexity for Weakly Convex Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2608.03246v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the oracle complexity of finding $\epsilon$-stationary points of $\rho$-weakly convex and $G$-Lipschitz functions, where stationarity is measured by the gradient norm of the Moreau envelope. We consider an exact first-order oracle that returns both the function value and the full subdifferential at every query point. For sufficiently small $\epsilon>0$, we prove that every first-order algorithm, including randomized algorithms, requires $\Omega({\rho G^2\Delta}/{\epsilon^4})$ oracle queries to succeed with any fixed positive probability, where $f(0)-\inf f\le\Delta$. This lower bound matches the best known deterministic and stochastic first-order upper bounds, up to universal constants, and establishes the optimal randomized and deterministic first-order oracle complexity. The result separates smooth nonconvex and nonsmooth weakly convex optimization: the additional $\epsilon^{-2}$ factor is intrinsic to nonsmooth geometry rather than to stochastic oracle noise.
item.dc:creator: Jiajin Li, Siyu Pan

item.title: A Spectral Proximal DC Algorithm with Nonmonotone Line Search and Extrapolation
item.description: arXiv:2608.03465v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The paper proposes a novel proximal difference-of-convex (DC) algorithmic framework to solve general nonconvex, nonsmooth optimization problems. The basic pBBDCA method combines Barzilai-Borwein (BB) parameter selection with a nonmonotone directional line search, requiring only one proximal solve per iteration. We also develop two extrapolated variants using restart and safeguarding mechanisms. The global convergence of the proposed framework is rigorously established under the Kurdyka-\L ojasiewicz property. Numerical experiments on the SCAD-regularized least squares problem and graph Ginzburg-Landau image segmentation models demonstrate that the proposed methods achieve highly competitive efficiency and accuracy.
item.dc:creator: Kelin Wu, Hongpeng Sun

item.title: Accelerating Stochastic Gradient Method Using Large Stepsize for Smooth Strongly Convex Minimization
item.description: arXiv:2608.15035v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study predetermined stepsize schedules for stochastic gradient methods on m-strongly convex, M-smooth objectives with conditionally unbiased gradient estimates and bounded conditional variance. We derive an exact tight analysis on every schedule with stepsizes in [0,2/(M+1)]. We then characterize the globally optimal one- and two-step schedules over all nonnegative stepsizes. Both optimal schedules depend on the ratio of the initial optimality gap to the noise level and exhibit several distinct regimes. As the influence of stochastic noise diminishes, the optimal stepsizes become larger, reflecting a balance between the benefits of faster iterate convergence and the perturbations induced by stochastic noise. These solutions motivate serial and silver composition rules with explicit performance bounds. For arbitrary horizons, we construct a schedule combining a balanced Silver prefix with constant and decreasing short steps, with the prefix length selected through explicit thresholds. Its certified upper bound never exceeds the exact optimum over all short-step schedules and is strictly smaller whenever a nonempty Silver prefix is selected. Finally, we prove global optimality of the proposed schedule on an explicit sufficient interval of the initial-error-to-variance ratio.
item.dc:creator: Luwei Bai, Baoyu Zhou

item.title: Let AEDs Move: Urban Mobility Enhanced Defibrillator Deployment
item.description: arXiv:2608.23810v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Early defibrillation is critical to survival after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA). However, public-access defibrillation programs rely largely on stationary automated external defibrillators (AEDs), whose fixed locations cannot adapt to spatial and temporal variation in OHCA demand and which a bystander must retrieve on foot. We study a platform-enabled deployment model in which ride-hailing vehicles carry AEDs that can be dispatched directly to OHCA locations. Holding total AED supply fixed, we evaluate the full range of allocations between stationary and mobile deployment. Our analysis draws on public AED inventories, EMS-reported OHCA incidents, and ride-hailing mobility data from New York City and Toronto. Reallocating part of the supply to vehicles substantially shortens AED response times, but the benefit is non-monotonic in the mobile share. Under a specification common to both cities, mean improvement reaches approximately 2.9 minutes in each, yet the preferred allocation differs: it peaks with 55% of AEDs mobile in Toronto, whereas New York City retains near-maximum gains across 40%-80%, with further variation across boroughs. The preferred allocation also depends on the response-time target, where coverage within 3 and 5 minutes favors greater mobility while 10-minute coverage favors retaining part of the stationary network. Toronto's vehicle-level data further show that targeting AEDs to active vehicles is essential and with such targeting, restricting dispatch to idle vehicles, which disrupts no passenger trip, does not reduce the gain, and allowing any active equipped vehicle to respond raises it to 5.7 minutes under full mobilization. Mobilizing AEDs can therefore materially improve access, and the stationary-mobile mix must be tailored to local coverage, fleet activity, and dispatch rules.
item.dc:creator: Bahar D Viniche, Sheng Liu, Nooshin Salari

item.title: An Adaptive Linesearch-free Method for Monotone Variational Inequalities under Local Lipschitz Continuity
item.description: arXiv:2609.15936v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The forward-reflected-backward (FRB) splitting solves monotone inclusions involving the sum of a maximally monotone operator and a monotone Lipschitz continuous operator. Each iteration performs one resolvent step and one evaluation of the Lipschitz operator, together with a reflection term with coefficient equal to one that reuses the operator value from the previous iteration. We consider the setting where the maximally monotone operator is the subdifferential of a proper, closed, convex function. We identify the admissible range of constant reflection coefficients, namely all values larger than one half for a sufficiently small stepsize. We then propose a linesearch-free adaptive variant of FRB for locally Lipschitz continuous operators, in which both the stepsize and the reflection coefficient change across iterations. The stepsize is computed in closed form from a simple local Lipschitz estimate, without knowledge of a global Lipschitz constant, while keeping the iteration cost of FRB. The analysis of both methods relies on a new Lyapunov function that combines the distance to a solution, a residual, and a gap-related term. Alongside nonasymptotic rates, we derive explicit lower bounds on the generated stepsizes, and report numerical experiments on minimax problems, equilibrium models, and regularized regression.
item.dc:creator: Hongjia Ou, Andreas Themelis, Puya Latafat

item.title: DREAM: Delay-Resistant Acceleration with Momentum
item.description: arXiv:2610.37444v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: With exact, delay-free gradients, Nesterov's accelerated gradient (NAG) achieves optimal $\sqrt{\kappa}$ dependence for $L$-smooth, $\mu$-strongly convex objectives, where $\kappa=L/\mu$; heavy-ball (HB) achieves the same scaling on strongly convex quadratics. In asynchronous and distributed settings, gradients can be inexact, with delays varying across workers and iterations. We isolate staleness using a fixed delay $\tau\ge1$, replacing $\nabla f(y_k)$ with $\nabla f(y_{k-\tau})$ at iteration $k$. Arjevani, Shamir, and Srebro establish a worst-case lower bound of $\Omega(\tau\sqrt{\kappa}\log(1/\varepsilon))$ iterations to reach objective error at most $\varepsilon$ as $\varepsilon\to0$. We show that for any fixed positive delay, neither NAG nor HB retains $\sqrt{\kappa}$-acceleration on strongly convex quadratics when updating every iteration, for any stable constant step size and positive momentum. We introduce delay-resistant accelerated momentum (DREAM), which decouples gradient-query extrapolation from momentum and uses explicit delay-dependent parameters. DREAM attains a linear convergence rate $1-\Theta(1/(\tau\sqrt{\kappa}))$ for all smooth strongly convex objectives as $\kappa\to\infty$, yielding complexity matching the delayed first-order lower bound up to logarithmic factors. Our proof combines characteristic-polynomial stability analysis on quadratics with an analytic Zames--Falb integral quadratic constraint certificate. We extend DREAM to smooth convex objectives, obtaining near-optimal iteration complexity up to logarithmic factors for sufficiently small target accuracy. Experiments on strongly convex quadratics and regularized logistic regression corroborate DREAM's accelerated condition-number dependence under delay, unlike NAG and HB, and suggest this scaling persists when parameters use a conservative bound on the true delay.
item.dc:creator: Mert G\"urb\"uzbalaban, M. Hamza Rafi, Necdet Serhat Aybat, Waheed U. Bajwa

item.title: Costate-Conditioned Dynamic Programming for Parallel-in-Time Solution of Equality-Constrained Optimal Control Problems
item.description: arXiv:2611.10286v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Gradient based trajectory optimisation algorithms spend most of their per-iteration time on a structured Newton--KKT system. The system corresponds to an equality-constrained linear-quadratic optimal control problem and dedicated Riccati-type solvers exhibit linear complexity in the horizon length. Parallel-in-time algorithms exhibit the potential to reduce the complexity to logarithmic in the horizon by distributing several subtrajectories over multiple cores and then stitch together the results by means of an associative scan. Existing exact formulations condition each subtrajectory on its terminal state. Each subproblem then carries the reachability to that terminal state explicitly as constraint rows. The associated reachability decision however is ill-conditioned for weakly actuated systems. In this work we condition each subtrajectory on the terminal costate instead. The resulting subproblems can now be computed by a free-end Riccati recursion without reachability carrying rows. This approach effectively compensates for the ill-conditioning of weakly actuated systems but requires additional bookkeeping with Lagrangian multipliers when stitching together the various subproblems. Numerically the method reproduces a direct solution of the primal-dual Newton-KKT system to $10^{-12}$ in relative terms, on a weakly controllable chain of masses. The accurracy rivals that of a sequential recursion, whereas terminal-state conditioning loses up to six digits or fails. Operation counts on a problem with 64 subtrajectories and a horizon of 4096 stages gives a speed-up of 26 compared with a sequential solve.
item.dc:creator: Tom Lefebvre

item.title: Information geometric regularization of unidimensional pressureless Euler equations yields global strong solutions
item.description: arXiv:2411.15121v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Partial differential equations describing compressible fluids are prone to the formation of shock singularities, arising from faster upstream fluid particles catching up to slower, downstream ones. In geometric terms, this causes the deformation map to leave the manifold of diffeomorphisms. Information geometric regularization addresses this issue by changing the manifold geometry to make it geodesically complete. Empirical evidence suggests that this results in smooth solutions without adding artificial viscosity. This work makes a first step towards understanding this phenomenon rigorously, in the setting of the unidimensional pressureless Euler equations. It shows that their information geometric regularization has smooth global solutions. By establishing $\Gamma$-convergence of its variational description, it proves convergence of these solutions to entropy solutions of the nominal problem, in the limit of vanishing regularization parameter. A consequence of these results is that manifolds of unidimensional diffeomorphisms with information geometric regularization are geodesically complete.
item.dc:creator: Ruijia Cao, Florian Sch\"afer

item.title: Simultaneous Learning and Optimization via Misspecified Saddle Point Problems
item.description: arXiv:2510.05241v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study a class of misspecified saddle point (SP) problems, where the optimization objective depends on an unknown parameter that must be learned concurrently from data. Unlike existing studies that assume parameters are fully known or pre-estimated, our framework integrates optimization and learning into a unified formulation, enabling a more flexible problem class. To address this setting, we propose two algorithms based on the accelerated primal-dual (APD) by Hamedani & Aybat 2021. In particular, we first analyze the naive extension of the APD method by directly substituting the evolving parameter estimates into the primal-dual updates; then, we design a new learning-aware variant of the APD method that explicitly accounts for parameter dynamics by adjusting the momentum updates. Both methods achieve a provable convergence rate of $\mathcal{O}(\log K / K)$, while the learning-aware approach attains a tighter $\mathcal{O}(1)$ constant and further benefits from an adaptive step-size selection enabled by a backtracking strategy. Furthermore, we extend the framework to problems where the learning problem admits multiple optimal solutions, showing that our modified algorithm for a structured setting achieves an $\mathcal{O}(1/\sqrt{K})$ rate. To demonstrate practical impact, we evaluate our methods on a misspecified portfolio optimization problem and show superior empirical performance compared to state-of-the-art algorithms.
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Mahdi Ahmadi, Erfan Yazdandoost Hamedani

item.title: Analytically Characterized Optimal Power Control for Signal-Level-Integrated Sensing, Computing and Communication in Federated Learning
item.description: arXiv:2604.26741v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In next-generation wireless edge systems, efficient functionality integration is essential to address the growing demands of communication, computation, and sensing. Signal-level integrated sensing, computing, and communication (Sig-ISCC) is envisioned, where a single waveform simultaneously supports sensing, computing and communication via over-the-air computation (AirComp). Meanwhile, federated learning (FL) is widely regarded as a promising distributed machine learning framework that enables network intelligence in a privacy-preserving and secure manner, and exhibits strong synergy with AirComp, which alleviates the communication bottleneck of FL. In this paper, we study uplink Sig-ISCC design for AirComp-FL with joint target detection. We formulate the joint power and receive-scaling control problem, where edge devices' transmitted signals should serve both sensing and AirComp purposes. The goal is to minimize the AirComp aggregation distortion subject to a joint target-detection requirement. Although the resulting problem is non-convex in the original variables, we show that it admits an equivalent convex reformulation after a suitable variable transformation. By exploiting analytical optimality properties, we develop a robust, optimal, and polynomial-time-complexity algorithm that efficiently achieves the optimal transmit powers and receive scaling factor. Simulation results validate the optimality and numerical robustness of the proposed algorithm and show its superior FL performance compared to baseline methods.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: IEEE Transactions on Wireless Communications, vol. 25, pp. 25941-25958, 2026
item.dc:creator: Paul Zheng, Yao Zhu, Xiaopeng Yuan, Yulin Hu, Anke Schmeink

item.title: Match classification in the last round of four-team round-robin tournaments
item.description: arXiv:2605.25610v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Classification of matches played in the last rounds of sports competitions is a well-established tool for evaluating tournament designs. Our paper offers the first comparison of deterministic and probabilistic match classification models by analysing the most prominent example of four-team round-robin competitions, the group stage of the FIFA World Cup. We show that both models are highly relevant in practice: all (four) deterministic and (six) probabilistic match types occurred in the 2014 and 2018 FIFA World Cups, respectively. The probabilistic model, which accounts for the relative benefits of attacking and defending, provides a deeper insight; for instance, the competitive matches from the deterministic approach can be of any of the six probabilistic types. Therefore, the probabilistic model is used to decompose the impact of three reforms introduced in the 2026 FIFA World Cup: the expansion to 48 teams, the modified qualification rules, and head-to-head tie-breakers.
item.dc:creator: L\'aszl\'o Csat\'o, Andr\'as Gyimesi

item.title: Eigenvalues of locally positive semidefinite matrices: Non-convexity and Geometry
item.description: arXiv:2608.15444v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A real symmetric matrix is called $d$-locally positive semidefinite if all of its $d \times d$ principal submatrices are positive semidefinite. We investigate the spectral geometry of $d$-locally positive semidefinite matrices. The set of vectors of eigenvalues of $d$-locally positive semidefinite matrices of size $n \times n$ is fully understood and known to be convex when $d \in \{1,n-1,n\}$ \cite{blekherman2022hyperbolic}. In the smallest remaining case $n=4, d=2$, non-convexity of the set of vectors of eigenvalues was proved in \cite{kozhasov2023eigenvalues}, but even in this case the full description was unknown. We provide a basic semialgebraic description of the set of vectors of eigenvalues for $n=4, d=2$ by establishing a Fischer-type inequality for $2$-locally positive semidefinite matrices of size $4 \times 4$. We prove non-convexity for all $n \geq 4$ and $2 \leq d \leq n - 2$. For $d=2$ we prove a natural linear inequality on a linear slice of eigenvalues of locally positive semidefinite matrices which is tight at exactly two points. This gives a stronger proof of non-convexity in this case. For $d \in \{2, n - 2\}$, analyzing this slice involves solving certain non-smooth and non-convex min-max point configuration problems in the complex plane, which could be of independent interest. Similar problems were considered in \cite{nesterenko2024submatrices,sengupta2026submatrices} in the context of matrix decomposition and approximation.
item.dc:creator: Jose Acevedo, Grigoriy Blekherman, Sebastian Debus, Seokbin Lee, Cordian Riener

item.title: A Theory of Information Architecture for Networked Decisions: Freshness, Locality, and Coordination
item.description: arXiv:2609.06351v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A broader view of a network can help agents coordinate, but collecting that view takes time. When is a fresh local observation more useful than an older view of the whole network, and when should an agent look only partway across it? We study agents that repeatedly minimize a shared quadratic cost in an environment that evolves independently of their actions. An information architecture specifies what each agent observes and how old those observations are. Each agent uses a synchronized neighborhood snapshot, so extending its scope also ages the nearby readings used in the decision. We assume that the optimal action with complete information is affine in the state, and that the conditional mean of the current state equals the old state scaled by a common exponential decay factor. Using the classical Marschak--Radner decomposition, we derive the delay threshold beyond which fresh local information outperforms a complete but older global view. This comparison allows non-Gaussian states and nonlinear decision rules. We then determine how far an agent should look by balancing the benefit of additional observations against their greater age. In a Gaussian spatial model on a line, we derive the optimal observation radius: looking beyond the local node pays only when information travels more than twice the spatial correlation length in one coherence time. The preferred information architecture also depends on the decision being made. On a fixed 64-node ring, increasing only the reach of the decision weights from 0.7 to 6 hops shifts the optimal observation radius from one to five hops.
item.dc:creator: Scott Moeller, Bhaskar Krishnamachari

item.title: A Convex-Analytic Reformulation for Poisoning Attacks on Logistic Regression
item.description: arXiv:2611.17143v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study data poisoning attacks on logistic regression with $\ell_2$-regularization, where an attacker chooses the features of a fixed number of injected observations with prescribed labels to maximize the logistic loss on the clean training data. Strong convexity of the defender's problem yields an exact reformulation through its first-order optimality conditions. Using convex conjugacy of the softplus function, we replace the sigmoid relations by a single convex optimality-gap inequality and express the attacker's objective as a concave function. A change of variables makes the stationarity condition affine, leaving bounded bilinear equalities as the only nonconvex constraints. We derive finite bounds on all variables involved in these equalities, including a global bound on the coefficient norm and tighter bounds obtained by preprocessing based on convex optimization. Experiments on eight binary classification datasets evaluate attack effectiveness and compare the two reformulations when solved with SCIP. Attacks obtained by local optimization degrade predictive performance on most datasets, while the convex-analytic formulation produces substantially stronger reported dual bounds within a fixed time limit.
item.dc:creator: Carina Moreira Costa, Maria Eduarda Pinheiro, Martin Schmidt
